property: The many-serial-ports-to-network edge role expands from interactive terminal/session attachment into subscriber-link termination that negotiates SLIP/PPP, authenticates users and attaches them as routed IP endpoints.

date_or_range.notes: DECserver 100/LAT represents a mature LAN terminal-server role; Cisco 1992 documents router/terminal-server convergence; Livingston 1995 documents PPP/SLIP dial access.

sources.locator: DEC LAT Architecture Network Manager's Guide, DECserver 100 documentation/product environment
sources.supports: LAN terminal-server role and DECserver/LAT architecture
contemporary commercial convergence of terminal-server and remote-router roles
sources.notes: Important bridge evidence between category labels, not proof of DEC-to-Cisco product descent.

sources.locator: PortMaster configuration guide, SLIP/PPP and PAP/CHAP sections
sources.supports: dial access server terminating serial subscriber links, negotiating IP link protocols and authenticating users

negative_claims: This edge does not claim Livingston PortMaster hardware or source code derives from DECserver hardware/software.
This edge does not claim X.25 PAD, LAT terminal server and PPP access server use one continuous wire protocol.
This edge does not imply that terminal servers disappeared when dial access servers became common; roles coexisted and products often combined them.
open_questions: Trace specific commercial product-family transitions from terminal server to communications/access server.
Recover Cisco STS/MSM/ASM/500-CS configuration manuals and hardware BOMs.

Identify earlier TCP/IP terminal servers supporting SLIP/PPP before PortMaster and compare roles.
Build a port/session/authentication responsibility matrix across TIP, PAD, DECserver and access servers.
notes: Reference example of role genealogy: a recurring edge function gains new protocol and authentication responsibilities without requiring direct vendor or source-code ancestry.
